title: Missing Number
keyIdea: nums holds n distinct numbers from 0..n, so exactly one is missing. Three O(n), O(1) ways: cyclic sort (put each value at its own index, then find the gap), total − sum, or XOR every index with every value so all but the missing one cancel.

approaches.name: Sort + scan
approaches.idea: Your commented version: sort, return the first i with nums[i] != i, else n.

approaches.name: Sort + binary search
approaches.idea: Your commented version: after sorting, nums[mid] == mid means the gap is to the right; find the first index where it breaks.
approaches.why: The sort dominates; the search itself is O(log n).

approaches.name: XOR indexes and values
approaches.idea: I added this one (the bit-manipulation answer): ans = n; ans ^= i ^ nums[i] for every i.
approaches.why: One pass; every present number cancels with its index.

approaches.name: Sum formula
approaches.idea: Your commented "better" version: n(n + 1)/2 − sum of nums.

approaches.name: Cyclic sort
approaches.idea: Your active code: swap nums[i] into index nums[i] (skip the value n), then the first index i with nums[i] != i is missing; else n.
approaches.why: Each swap fixes one value for good, so at most n swaps plus n steps of i. It changes the input array.
